review_mode: Scheduled cloud dual-review; independent Codex desk
limitations: Confidence values are subjective evidence confidence, not return probabilities. News remains unweighted in the trading score.

Only material new or materially changed evidence is reviewed in this run. Re-publication of the previously reviewed Qatari LNG cargo was recognized as the same story and was not re-rated merely because a fresh article repeated it.

The ATRL item is an Intermarket Securities initiation/report carried by Mettis Global, not a new ATRL corporate filing. It is therefore treated as direct company evidence but only correlated for score-bearing causality.

The FY26 auto-assembler article is a backward-looking aggregation of already-filed company accounts. It is reviewed as positive sector context but not applied as a sector score because the compiled set excludes HCAR, while the repository currently maps GHNI to Glass/Holding even though PSX classifies GHNI as an Automobile Assembler.
The fresh petrol/HSD reset leaves the OMC margin unchanged at Rs7.87/litre; it does not resolve the separate outstanding OMC price-differential and margin-implementation issues reviewed previously.

reviewed_stories.title: ATRL eyes profit expansion as capacity utilization, product yields recover
reviewed_stories.linkage_detail: Direct company analysis for Attock Refinery Limited (PSX: ATRL), verified against the PSX company profile.
reviewed_stories.reason: The full article cites FY26 EPS of Rs207.32 versus Rs112.29 in FY25 and an Intermarket Securities view that higher northern crude availability, improving utilization and the brownfield upgrade could lift product yields and profitability. The evidence is positive, but much of the upside is forecast-dependent rather than a newly disclosed corporate event.
reviewed_stories.publication_time_status: Mettis Global article clock states September 21, 2026 at 04:55 PM GMT+05:00.

reviewed_stories.title: Oil price dips to USD100
reviewed_stories.linkage_detail: Sector linkage to tracked upstream producers OGDC, PPL and MARI through realized hydrocarbon prices.
reviewed_stories.reason: Brent settled at $100.34, down 3.4% and at its lowest since September 9, as diplomacy hopes and partial Saudi shipment recovery reduced the war-risk premium. This materially weakens, but does not fully remove, the positive upstream price backdrop carried from the prior session.
reviewed_stories.publication_time_status: Business Recorder shows Published September 22, 2026 05:15am PKT.

reviewed_stories.title: Petrol price up by Rs4.61, HSD's down by Rs1.96
reviewed_stories.linkage_detail: Sector linkage to Oil Marketing, including PSO, through regulated retail prices and OMC per-litre margins.
